tara: Heads-up — the new edge ESM sample we ship for onboarding is producing broken inference in consuming apps. When consumers import the SDK via the ESM entry, generic return types collapse to `any` or `unknown`. Runtime works, so this is purely typing.

leo: which tsconfig are you seeing this with?

tara: consumer uses TS 5.3, module: "esnext", moduleResolution: "bundler", target: "es2022", esModuleInterop: false. Minimal repro attached to the ticket.

anita: can you paste the SDK signatures that are mis-inferred?

tara: simplified SDK shape below:
```ts
// in @redwood/sdk (before bundling)
export declare function request<T>(path: string, opts?: ReqOpts): Promise<T>
export declare function request(path: string, opts?: ReqOpts): Promise<any>
```
Consumer ends up with `Promise<any>` even when they call `request<User>(...)`.

mike: ugh, classic overload + emit reorder. I bet our build step transforms `export declare function` into a `const request = wrap(requestImpl)` pattern and the dts emitter writes a `const request: any` or reorders overloads, losing the generic.

leo: quick experiment: if you hand-edit a types file that uses `declare function request<T>(...)` and consumers compile, then it's definitely an emitter problem.

tara: confirmed — manual .d.ts with `declare function` preserves inference.

anita: short-term mitigation ideas: (a) ship a preserved types-only d.ts for the ESM edge package that keeps `declare function` signatures, (b) add an example tsconfig in onboarding for edge targets (moduleResolution: bundler + a note to avoid mixing `nodeNext` unless consumers are using node loader), (c) add a small CI compile check where we run `tsc --noEmit` on a consumer sample with the bundler matrix.

mike: long-term: refactor away from overlapping overloads. Consider a single generic API with discriminated options so there's no ambiguous overload selection. Also ensure our wrapper factory exposes a typed signature via `declare function` + `export { request }` rather than `const`.

leo: also watch out for `preserveValueImports` and `isolatedModules` interactions in downstream bundlers — they can influence how TS treats the import shape. Add a note in the onboarding doc about common gotchas and recommended flags.

tara: agreed. I'll open a ticket with the minimal repro and the failing `tsc --noEmit` invocation. please avoid recommending `skipLibCheck` as a fix — it hides real regressions.

devex-bot: Created ticket INF-8567: "edge ESM types: overloaded signatures collapse to any/unknown" — assignee: @mike — priority: P2 :thumbsup:

mike: I'll take INF-8567. Plan: (1) produce preserved types artifact for ESM edge, (2) add a CI compile matrix test, (3) prototype single-signature refactor for the most-used APIs. Anyone want to pair on (1)?

anita: I can pair tomorrow morning for 30 mins.

tara: thanks all — adding the repro link and the exact tsconfig to the ticket now.
